source.repro: products/jbrowse-web: node browser-tests/probe-per-base-bin.ts --out=<dir> against two builds of jbrowse-web, then --diff <before> <after>. The before arm is `perBaseBinBp` in plugins/alignments/src/LinearAlignmentsDisplay/model.ts edited to return 1; it is flipped locally, rebuilt, captured, and put back, and nothing in the tree carries a changed value. Headless Chrome on SwiftShader at a pinned 1280x800 viewport (so dpr is 1), volvox ctgA, volvox_alignments, capturing the pileup display's canvas.
source.notes: Read the two control rows first: colour-by-normal never reaches the per-base extract, and per-base quality at 0.8 bp/px is the same colour mode at a zoom where subPixelBinBp returns 1 in BOTH arms. Both come back byte-identical, so the capture is stable and every other row is the bin. `differing` counts any pixel whose max per-channel delta is nonzero and overstates what is visible; `colourTV` is total-variation distance between the two arms' colour histograms over inked pixels, and `saturatedAfter` minus `saturatedBefore` is the finding — the share of inked pixels with HSV saturation above 0.55. `inkDelta` is the change in inked-pixel count, i.e. whether the wall lost coverage; it does not. Mechanism: both backends floor a per-base cell to 1 CSS px, so ~38 cells composite into each pixel at 37.9 bp/px before the bin and ~2.4 after. A narrow colour ramp survives that; four separated hues do not.
